passages.provision_quote: A person, committee, or other entity shall not, during the time period set forth in subdivision (c), with malice, knowingly distribute an advertisement or other election communication containing materially deceptive content of any of the following:
passages.note: The prohibition runs against the person or committee that distributes election deepfakes, not against platforms, and the bill expressly disclaims liability for interactive computer services.
passages.actor_quote: AB 2839, Pellerin. Elections: deceptive media in advertisements.

rows.reasoning: Pellerin authored AB 2839 (2023-2024), which bars a person, committee or other entity from knowingly distributing election advertisements with materially deceptive content, and which states that "This section does not impose liability on an interactive computer service, as defined in Section 230(f)(2) of Title 47 of the United States Code." Every rung of this ladder turns on what platforms must do or on government involvement in content moderation — "legally require platforms to remove false information", "require platforms to label false content, rather than remove it", "encourage voluntary standards for combating misinformation online" — and a distributor-liability statute that exempts platforms establishes none of them. No surviving passage speaks to the dimension the rungs separate, so the row is blank.
